claims.text: Age: the patient must be at least 21 years old when consent is obtained, and not declared mentally incompetent.
claims.quote: (a) The individual is at least 21 years old at the time consent is obtained. (b) The individual is not a mentally incompetent individual.

claims.text: Waiting period: at least 30 days but not more than 180 days between consent and the sterilization.
claims.quote: At least 30 days but not more than 180 days have passed between the date of informed consent and the date of the sterilization

claims.text: Exception: with premature delivery or emergency abdominal surgery, sterilization may be done if at least 72 hours have passed since consent; for premature delivery, consent must have been given at least 30 days before the expected delivery date.
claims.quote: An individual may consent to be sterilized at the time of premature delivery or emergency abdominal surgery, if at least 72 hours have passed after he or she gave informed consent to sterilization. In the case of premature delivery, the informed consent must have been given at least 30 days before the expected date of delivery.

claims.text: Not valid when obtained: in labor or childbirth, while seeking or obtaining an abortion, or under the influence of alcohol or other substances that affect awareness.
claims.quote: (e) Informed consent may not be obtained while the individual to be sterilized is: (1) In labor or childbirth; (2) Seeking to obtain or obtaining an abortion; or (3) Under the influence of alcohol or other substances that affect the individual's state of awareness.

claims.text: What to tell the patient: they may withdraw consent any time before the procedure without losing future care or benefits; the alternative birth control methods; that the procedure is considered irreversible; its risks and benefits; and that it will not be done for at least 30 days (except as above).
claims.quote: (1) Advice that the individual is free to withhold or withdraw consent to the procedure any time before the sterilization without affecting his or her right to future care or treatment and without loss or withdrawal of any federally funded program benefits to which the individual might be otherwise entitled: (2) A description of available alternative methods of family planning and birth control; (3) Advice that the sterilization procedure is considered to be irreversible; (4) A thorough explanation of the specific sterilization procedure to be performed; (5) A full description of the discomforts and risks that may accompany or follow the performing of the procedure, including an explanation of the type and possible effects of any anesthetic to be used; (6) A full description of the benefits or advantages that may be expected as a result of the sterilization; and (7) Advice that the sterilization will not be performed for at least 30 days except under the circumstances specified in § 50.203(d) of this subpart.

claims.text: Interpreter: provide one if the patient doesn't understand the language of the consent form or of the person obtaining consent.
claims.quote: (b) An interpreter must be provided to assist the individual to be sterilized if he or she does not understand the language used on the consent form or the language used by the person obtaining the consent.

claims.text: State law, not spousal consent: follow any state or local consent requirement, except a requirement for spousal consent.
claims.quote: (f) Any requirement of State and local law for obtaining consent, except one of spousal consent, must be followed.
